correctness.rationale: The periodic squared-distance proof counts precisely one vertex maximum per side-interior foot minimum. Opposite cyclic chords have coincident centered side-foot slabs, forcing the three atoms; the known Hug expectation eight forces symmetric extreme probabilities. In an obtuse noncyclic hexagon at least one nonpaired foot-strip boundary enters the interior and induces an isolated count jump by two, proving the contrapositive rigidity. The exact regular and nonregular polygon areas were independently reconstructed, and the delivered standard-library checker reproduces 290,000 seeded geometric comparisons. Finite tests do not prove infinite statements.

value.rationale: This is a natural, complete distributional classification for the smallest nontrivial centrally symmetric cyclic polygon beyond a parallelogram, relevant to fluctuations of static-equilibrium counts as the reference point varies. The geometric parity criterion detects cyclicity in the full strictly-obtuse centrally symmetric hexagonal family, while the regular equidistribution and nonregular exact ratio are shape-sensitive, non-implied facts that the preceding expectation theorem alone cannot supply.
